content.heading: Defamation
content.text: A person commits the tort of defamation by publishing to a third party a false statement that refers to the claimant and tends to lower the claimant in the estimation of right-thinking members of society or to expose the claimant to hatred, contempt, or ridicule. Publication may be in permanent form (libel) or transient form (slander), subject to rules on when slander is actionable without special damage. Defences include justification (truth), fair comment on a matter of public interest, and absolute or qualified privilege. Consent and offer of amends may also be relevant. Civil defamation is distinct from the criminal offence of defamation.
